scope: Leviticus 1–3, all 50 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Leviticus 1–3.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Makes the LORD explicit as caller and speaker, retaining the tent location that connects to Exodus’ ending.
verses.before: The LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying,
verses.after: The LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps general human scope, offering repetition and herd/flock restriction without narrowing all offerings to male worshipers.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When any one of you brings an offering to the LORD from the livestock, you may bring your offering from the herd or from the flock.
verses.after: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When any of you brings an offering to the LORD from your livestock, bring your offering from the herd or the flock.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When any one of you brings an offering to the LORD from the livestock, you may bring your offering from the herd or from the flock.

verses.rationale: Retains animal’s specific male sex and wholeness, while reading acceptance rather than imposing voluntariness on lirṣono.
verses.before: If the offering is a burnt offering from the herd, the person will present a male without defect. It will be presented at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting so that it may be accepted before the LORD.
verses.after: If the offering is a burnt offering from the herd, the person bringing it must present a male without defect. They must present it at the entrance to the tent of meeting, for acceptance before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the offering is a burnt offering from the herd, the person shall present a male without defect. It shall be presented at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting so that it may be accepted before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves hand contact, acceptance and atonement without adding a theory of transfer or an unmentioned confession.
verses.before: The person will lay a hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted on that person’s behalf to make atonement.
verses.after: They are to lay a hand on the burnt offering’s head, and it will be accepted on their behalf to make atonement for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The person shall lay a hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted on that person’s behalf to make atonement.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the offerer’s slaughter from priests’ blood presentation and splashing, matching Exodus’ blood-action terminology.
verses.before: The bull will be slaughtered before the LORD. Aaron’s sons, the priests, will bring forward the blood and dash the blood against all sides of the altar at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: They must slaughter the bull before the LORD. Aaron’s sons, the priests, are to present the blood and splash it against all sides of the altar at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: The bull shall be slaughtered before the LORD. Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall bring forward the blood and dash the blood against all sides of the altar at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Keeps offerer as continuing agent and both concrete preparation actions.
verses.before: The burnt offering will be skinned and cut into its pieces.
verses.after: The person bringing the burnt offering is to skin it and cut it into pieces.
verses.tsw_comparator: The burnt offering shall be skinned and cut into its pieces.

verses.rationale: Retains Aaron’s title, his sons as agents, and fire/wood order.
verses.before: The sons of Aaron the priest will put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
verses.after: The sons of Aaron the priest are to put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.

verses.rationale: Preserves pieces, head and fat distinctly, with nested wood/fire/altar relations.
verses.before: Aaron’s sons, the priests, will arrange the pieces, the head, and the fat upon the wood that is on the fire on the altar.
verses.after: Aaron’s sons, the priests, are to arrange the pieces, the head, and the fat on the wood over the fire on the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall arrange the pieces, the head, and the fat upon the wood that is on the fire on the altar.

verses.rationale: Clarifies washing versus priestly burning and retains all scope and offering-by-fire/aroma terminology consistent with Exodus; vocabulary notes the alternate food-gift sense.
verses.before: The entrails and legs will be washed with water. Then the priest will turn all of it into smoke on the altar as a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.after: The person bringing the offering must wash its entrails and legs with water. The priest is to burn all of it on the altar as a burnt offering, an offering by fire with a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The entrails and legs shall be washed with water. Then the priest shall turn all of it into smoke on the altar as a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains both flock species and specifically male unblemished animal without importing cattle’s entrance wording.
verses.before: If the offering is from the flock—from the sheep or from the goats—as a burnt offering, the person will present a male without defect.
verses.after: If the burnt offering comes from the flock, from sheep or goats, the person bringing it must present a male without defect.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the offering is from the flock—from the sheep or from the goats—as a burnt offering, the person shall present a male without defect.

verses.rationale: Keeps north orientation unique to this instruction and separates slaughterer from blood-handling priests.
verses.before: It will be slaughtered on the north side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron’s sons, the priests, will dash its blood against all sides of the altar.
verses.after: They must slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the LORD. Aaron’s sons, the priests, are to splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be slaughtered on the north side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall dash its blood against all sides of the altar.

verses.rationale: Preserves offerer’s cutting and priest’s arrangement, taking head/fat with the arranged pieces.
verses.before: It will be cut into its pieces, with its head and its fat, and the priest will arrange them upon the wood that is on the fire on the altar.
verses.after: The person bringing the offering is to cut it into pieces. The priest must arrange these, together with the head and fat, on the wood over the fire on the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be cut into its pieces, with its head and its fat, and the priest shall arrange them upon the wood that is on the fire on the altar.

verses.rationale: Retains present-all action in addition to burning and repeats species-closing formula intact.
verses.before: The entrails and the legs will be washed with water. The priest will present all of it and turn it into smoke on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.after: The person bringing the offering must wash the entrails and legs with water. The priest is to present all of it and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering by fire with a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The entrails and the legs shall be washed with water. The priest shall present all of it and turn it into smoke on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves bird alternatives and young qualifier only for pigeons, without adding a poverty condition here.
verses.before: If the offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, the person will bring the offering from turtledoves or young pigeons.
verses.after: If the burnt offering brought to the LORD is a bird, the offering must be a turtledove or a young pigeon.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, the person shall bring the offering from turtledoves or young pigeons.

verses.rationale: Keeps priestly killing and draining distinct from mammal blood splashing; names the head as burned before the body is prepared.
verses.before: The priest will bring it to the altar, pinch off its head, and turn the head into smoke on the altar. Its blood will be drained against the side of the altar.
verses.after: The priest is to bring it to the altar, wring off its head, and burn the head on the altar. Its blood is to be drained against the side of the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall bring it to the altar, pinch off its head, and turn the head into smoke on the altar. Its blood shall be drained against the side of the altar.

verses.rationale: Chooses crop/contents with alternate feathers sense noted; retains east side and disposal site.
verses.before: The priest will remove its crop with its contents and throw it beside the altar on the east side, in the place for ashes.
verses.after: He is to remove its crop with its contents and throw it beside the altar on the east side, where the ashes are placed.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall remove its crop with its contents and throw it beside the altar on the east side, in the place for ashes.

verses.rationale: Preserves tearing without full division, material placement and exact closing refrain; quote closure is an editorial chapter boundary.
verses.before: The priest will tear it open by its wings without dividing it completely. Then the priest will turn it into smoke on the altar, upon the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.after: The priest is to tear the bird open by its wings without separating it completely. Then the priest must burn it on the altar, on the wood over the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering by fire with a pleasing aroma to the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall tear it open by its wings without dividing it completely. Then the priest shall turn it into smoke on the altar, upon the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps anyone scope, flour/oil/frankincense and distinct grain-offering category without reducing nephesh to an immaterial soul.
verses.before: When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, the offering will be fine flour. The person will pour oil on it and place frankincense on it,
verses.after: “When someone brings a grain offering to the LORD, the offering must be fine flour. They are to pour oil on it and add frankincense.
verses.tsw_comparator: When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, the offering shall be fine flour. The person shall pour oil on it and place frankincense on it,

verses.rationale: Clarifies priest as the understood handful-taking agent, retaining full handful, all incense and memorial portion; notes unexpressed subject.
verses.before: and bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests. The priest will take from it a handful of the fine flour and oil, together with all its frankincense, and turn its memorial portion into smoke on the altar, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.after: They are to bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests. The priest is to take a handful of its flour and oil, along with all its frankincense, and burn this memorial portion on the altar—an offering by fire with a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: and bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests. The priest shall take from it a handful of the fine flour and oil, together with all its frankincense, and turn its memorial portion into smoke on the altar, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves priestly remainder, superlative holiness and relation to offerings rather than implying total altar consumption.
verses.before: What remains of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is most holy from the offerings by fire to the LORD.
verses.after: The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy part of the LORD’s offerings by fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: What remains of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is most holy from the offerings by fire to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains oven, fine flour, two baked forms, and distinct mixed/spread oil treatment.
verses.before: When you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it will be unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers spread with oil.
verses.after: If you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it must be fine flour made into unleavened cakes mixed with oil or unleavened wafers spread with oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it shall be unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers spread with oil.

verses.rationale: Preserves separate griddle method and flour/oil/no-leaven requirements.
verses.before: If your offering is a grain offering prepared on a griddle, it will be fine flour mixed with oil and unleavened.
verses.after: If your grain offering is prepared on a griddle, it must be fine flour mixed with oil and made without leaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: If your offering is a grain offering prepared on a griddle, it shall be fine flour mixed with oil and unleavened.

verses.rationale: Retains two ordered actions and repeated offering designation.
verses.before: Break it into pieces and pour oil on it. It is a grain offering.
verses.after: Break it into pieces and pour oil over it. It is a grain offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: Break it into pieces and pour oil on it. It is a grain offering.

verses.rationale: Keeps pan distinct from griddle, without importing no-leaven phrase before general prohibition.
verses.before: If your offering is a grain offering prepared in a pan, it will be made of fine flour with oil.
verses.after: If your grain offering is prepared in a pan, it must be made from fine flour with oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: If your offering is a grain offering prepared in a pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.

verses.rationale: Clarifies transfer from offerer to priest and movement to altar while retaining divine recipient.
verses.before: You will bring to the LORD the grain offering made from these things. It will be presented to the priest, who will bring it to the altar.
verses.after: Bring the grain offering made in any of these ways to the LORD. Present it to the priest, who is to bring it to the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall bring to the LORD the grain offering made from these things. It shall be presented to the priest, who shall bring it to the altar.

verses.rationale: Preserves removal of memorial portion, burning and recurring offering/aroma formula.
verses.before: The priest will lift from the grain offering its memorial portion and turn it into smoke on the altar, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.after: The priest is to take the memorial portion from the grain offering and burn it on the altar—an offering by fire with a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall lift from the grain offering its memorial portion and turn it into smoke on the altar, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains exact repetition of verse 3 because the remainder rule applies again after cooked preparations.
verses.before: What remains of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is most holy from the offerings by fire to the LORD.
verses.after: The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is a most holy part of the LORD’s offerings by fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: What remains of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is most holy from the offerings by fire to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves comprehensive leaven prohibition and leaven/honey burning restriction without extending it to all presentation.
verses.before: No grain offering that you bring to the LORD will be made with yeast, for you will not turn any yeast or any honey into smoke as an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.after: No grain offering you bring to the LORD may be made with leaven. You must not burn any leaven or honey as an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: No grain offering that you bring to the LORD shall be made with yeast, for you shall not turn any yeast or any honey into smoke as an offering by fire to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains leaven/honey referent and distinction between presentation and altar burning.
verses.before: You may bring them to the LORD as an offering of first produce, but they will not go up on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
verses.after: You may bring them to the LORD as an offering of first produce, but they must not go up on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
verses.tsw_comparator: You may bring them to the LORD as an offering of first produce, but they shall not go up on the altar as a pleasing aroma.

verses.rationale: Preserves threefold salt insistence, covenant relation and final broader all-offerings scope.
verses.before: You will season every grain offering with salt. You will not let the salt of the covenant of your God be missing from your grain offering. With every offering you will bring salt.
verses.after: Season every grain offering with salt. Do not leave the salt of your God’s covenant out of your grain offering. Bring salt with every offering you present.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall season every grain offering with salt. You shall not let the salt of the covenant of your God be missing from your grain offering. With every offering you shall bring salt.

verses.rationale: Keeps fresh/roasted/crushed grain descriptions and repeated firstfruits rather than forcing later-harvest flour into this preparation.
verses.before: If you bring a grain offering of first produce to the LORD, you will bring fresh heads of grain roasted in fire, crushed grain from the fresh crop, as the grain offering of your first produce.
verses.after: If you bring a grain offering of firstfruits to the LORD, bring fresh ears of grain roasted in the fire, crushed kernels of new grain, as your firstfruits offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you bring a grain offering of first produce to the LORD, you shall bring fresh heads of grain roasted in fire, crushed grain from the fresh crop, as the grain offering of your first produce.

verses.rationale: Preserves both additions and repeated category.
verses.before: You will put oil on it and place frankincense on it. It is a grain offering.
verses.after: Put oil on it and add frankincense. It is a grain offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall put oil on it and place frankincense on it. It is a grain offering.

verses.rationale: Retains partial grain/oil but all frankincense; does not add pleasing-aroma phrase absent in this closing verse.
verses.before: The priest will turn into smoke as its memorial portion some of the crushed grain and oil, together with all its frankincense. It is an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.after: The priest is to burn its memorial portion—some of its crushed grain and oil, along with all its frankincense—as an offering by fire to the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall turn into smoke as its memorial portion some of the crushed grain and oil, together with all its frankincense. It is an offering by fire to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Renders the sacrificial category as peace offering, matching Exodus; retains both animal sexes in contrast with chapter 1, and wholeness.
verses.before: If a person’s offering is a sacrifice of well-being, and it is offered from the herd, whether male or female, the person will present before the LORD an animal without defect.
verses.after: “If someone brings a peace offering from the herd, the animal presented before the LORD may be male or female, but it must be without defect.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a person’s offering is a sacrifice of well-being, and it is offered from the herd, whether male or female, the person shall present before the LORD an animal without defect.

verses.rationale: Clarifies offerer’s hand-laying/slaughter and priests’ blood role without assigning all actions to priest.
verses.before: The person will lay a hand on the head of the offering and slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Aaron’s sons, the priests, will dash the blood against all sides of the altar.
verses.after: The person bringing it is to lay a hand on its head and slaughter it at the entrance to the tent of meeting. Aaron’s sons, the priests, are to splash the blood against all sides of the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: The person shall lay a hand on the head of the offering and slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall dash the blood against all sides of the altar.

verses.rationale: Preserves two fat descriptions and begins a list continuing across the verse label.
verses.before: From the sacrifice of well-being the person will bring as an offering by fire to the LORD the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is around the entrails,
verses.after: From this peace offering, the person bringing it is to present these parts to the LORD as an offering by fire: the fat covering the entrails and all the fat on the entrails,
verses.tsw_comparator: From the sacrifice of well-being the person shall bring as an offering by fire to the LORD the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is around the entrails,

verses.rationale: Keeps paired kidneys, attached fat/location and provisional liver-lobe identification with alternate anatomy noted.
verses.before: the two kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the appendage of the liver, which will be removed with the kidneys.
verses.after: both kidneys and the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which they are to remove along with the kidneys.
verses.tsw_comparator: the two kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the appendage of the liver, which shall be removed with the kidneys.

verses.rationale: Preserves placement on the burnt offering and nested wood/fire relationship, rather than generic altar burning.
verses.before: Aaron’s sons will turn these into smoke on the altar, on top of the burnt offering that is on the wood over the fire. It is an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.after: Aaron’s sons are to burn these on the altar, on top of the burnt offering that rests on the wood over the fire—an offering by fire with a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron’s sons shall turn these into smoke on the altar, on top of the burnt offering that is on the wood over the fire. It is an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Repeats both sexes and wholeness for the separate flock category.
verses.before: If the offering to the LORD as a sacrifice of well-being is from the flock, whether male or female, the person will present an animal without defect.
verses.after: If the peace offering brought to the LORD comes from the flock, the animal may be male or female, but it must be without defect.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the offering to the LORD as a sacrifice of well-being is from the flock, whether male or female, the person shall present an animal without defect.

verses.rationale: Keeps sheep-specific branch and divine presentation without limiting to male lambs.
verses.before: If a lamb is brought as the offering, it will be presented before the LORD.
verses.after: If the offering is a sheep, the person bringing it must present it before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a lamb is brought as the offering, it shall be presented before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated hand/slaughter/blood sequence and sons without adding priest title absent here.
verses.before: The person will lay a hand on the head of the offering and slaughter it before the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron’s sons will dash its blood against all sides of the altar.
verses.after: They are to lay a hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting. Aaron’s sons are to splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: The person shall lay a hand on the head of the offering and slaughter it before the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron’s sons shall dash its blood against all sides of the altar.

verses.rationale: Keeps fat tail unique to sheep, entirety and near-backbone removal, then repeated inner-fat list.
verses.before: From the sacrifice of well-being the person will bring as an offering by fire to the LORD its fat: the entire fat tail, removed close to the backbone, the fat that covers the entrails, and all the fat around the entrails,
verses.after: From this peace offering, the person bringing it is to present its fat as an offering by fire to the LORD: the entire fat tail, cut off close to the backbone, the fat covering the entrails, and all the fat on the entrails,
verses.tsw_comparator: From the sacrifice of well-being the person shall bring as an offering by fire to the LORD its fat: the entire fat tail, removed close to the backbone, the fat that covers the entrails, and all the fat around the entrails,

verses.rationale: Retains exact anatomical recurrence and the same provisional lobe term as verse 4.
verses.before: the two kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the appendage of the liver, removed with the kidneys.
verses.after: both kidneys and the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which they are to remove along with the kidneys.
verses.tsw_comparator: the two kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the appendage of the liver, removed with the kidneys.

verses.rationale: Preserves explicit food image and absence of pleasing-aroma phrase in this verse without theological explanation.
verses.before: The priest will turn these into smoke on the altar as food, an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.after: The priest is to burn these on the altar as food, an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall turn these into smoke on the altar as food, an offering by fire to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps goat as distinct case and repeated presentation formula.
verses.before: If the offering is a goat, the person will present it before the LORD.
verses.after: If the offering is a goat, the person bringing it must present it before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the offering is a goat, the person shall present it before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves source repetition rather than replacing it with a reference back to sheep.
verses.before: The person will lay a hand on its head and slaughter it before the Tent of Meeting, and the sons of Aaron will dash its blood against all sides of the altar.
verses.after: They are to lay a hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting. Aaron’s sons are to splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: The person shall lay a hand on its head and slaughter it before the Tent of Meeting, and the sons of Aaron shall dash its blood against all sides of the altar.

verses.rationale: Keeps offerer’s contribution language and both fat descriptions without adding sheep’s tail.
verses.before: From it the person will bring as an offering by fire to the LORD the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat around the entrails,
verses.after: From the goat, the person bringing it is to present these parts as their offering by fire to the LORD: the fat covering the entrails and all the fat on the entrails,
verses.tsw_comparator: From it the person shall bring as an offering by fire to the LORD the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat around the entrails,

verses.rationale: Preserves third full anatomical list and consistent provisional terminology.
verses.before: the two kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the appendage of the liver, removed with the kidneys.
verses.after: both kidneys and the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which they are to remove along with the kidneys.
verses.tsw_comparator: the two kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the appendage of the liver, removed with the kidneys.

verses.rationale: Keeps food and aroma plus separate comprehensive claim of divine ownership.
verses.before: The priest will turn them into smoke on the altar as food, an offering by fire for a pleasing aroma. All the fat belongs to the LORD.
verses.after: The priest is to burn these on the altar as food, an offering by fire with a pleasing aroma. All the fat belongs to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall turn them into smoke on the altar as food, an offering by fire for a pleasing aroma. All the fat belongs to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains lasting/all-dwellings scope and comprehensive fat/blood prohibition, with ritual context explained selectively.
verses.before: This will be a perpetual statute throughout your generations, in all your dwellings: you will eat neither fat nor blood.”
verses.after: This is a lasting statute throughout your generations, wherever you live: you must not eat any fat or any blood.”
verses.tsw_comparator: This shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations, in all your dwellings: you shall eat neither fat nor blood.”
